To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

description.narrative:
Project did not have a results framework but worked to attain the results below 1.Expand national capacity for COVID- 19 testing and increased border surveillance and cross-border coordination.
a. Support the conducting of periodic rapid risk assessment and local level surveillance in hotspots for Covid-19 detection and reporting (coupled with the provision of a few bicycles/ motorcycles, on a pilot basis for increased mobility of community-based health workers in a few hotspots)
b. Provide a grant to Uganda Virus Research Institute to strengthen timely testing and collaboration between sub-national and national arms of the NECOC.
2. Strengthen national coordination capacities for emergency response and recovery with a robust Knowledge Management System for the National Emergency Coordination and Operations Centre.
a. Recruit and deploy a multidisciplinary team of four specialists (2 Disaster Risk and Resilience, 1 Knowledge Management, and 1 Emergency Communications Specialist) to form a core team to activate a think tank in NECOC. (one of the Disaster Risk and Resilience specialists will preferably have a bias in cross-border disaster risk coordination)
b. conduct strategic risk assessments
c. Prepare and disseminate analytical reports, policy briefs and best practices to inform policy, planning, budgeting and stakeholder engagement on COVID-19 and other disasters
d. Design a multi-sector strategy to inform short, medium and long-term capacity development for disaster risk reduction and mitigation.
e. Provide small grant funding to support research by members attached to the think-tank.

1. National capacity for COVID- 19 testing and border surveillance and cross-border coordination Increased.
a. Periodic rapid risk assessment and local level surveillance in hotspots for COVID-19 detection and reporting and provision of a few bicycles/ motorcycles for increased mobility of community-based health workers in few selected hotspots Supported
b. Grant to Uganda Virus Research Institute (UVRI) to strengthen timely testing and collaboration between sub-national and national arms of the National Emergency Coordination Operation Centre (NECOC) provided.
2. National coordination capacities for emergency response and recovery with a robust Knowledge Management System for the National Emergency Coordination and Operations Centre strengthened.
a. A multidisciplinary team of four specialists recruited and deployed.
c. Analytical reports, policy briefs and best practices to inform policy, planning, budgeting and stakeholder engagement on COVID-19 and other disasters prepared and disseminated.
d. A multi-sector strategy to inform short, medium and long-term capacity development for disaster risk reduction and mitigation designed.
e. A small grant funding to support research by members attached to the think-tank provided.

Results attained under indicator Number one (1) : • Built capacity of 32 Health workers (86% target) in 19-selected Health Facilities (HFs) in Central, Western, Eastern, Northern & West Nile sub-regions in community level sentinel surveillance. • Four new Border surveillance sentinel sites introduced and health workers trained and provided surveillance tools. • All sites were provided with supplies like Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) Antigen kits (100 kits @site), Personal Protective Equipment (PPEs) and logistics for community outreach. • Increased surveillance sentinel site reports shared bi-weekly with (National Emergency Coordination Operation Centre) NECOC for EW use. • Enhanced border surveillance made it possible for UVRI to detect (AH1NI) 2009 at the new border site of Bibia HCIII. • Six (6) Motorcycles procured to support 6 selected Health Centers in community and local level surveillance. • Community outreaches carried out and sensitized on surveillance of influenza, COVID-19, health education, etc.
a) Conducting of periodic rapid risk assessment and local level surveillance in hotspots for Covid-19 detection and reporting: - Finalized the 1st ever Rapid Needs Assessment Framework comprising of a set of tools namely; Pre-Disaster Assessment Tool, Rapid Needs Assessment Triger Sheet, Disaster Impact Rapid Needs Assessment Tool. - Wide consultation and input conducted for the Tools with select DDMCs, OPM-DRDPM Staff, National Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) Platform & a National multi-sector / Inter-agency workshop. -The tools were adopted by Office of the Prime Minister (OPM) and partners and currently under use in disaster assessments in Uganda. - A Health facility specific assessment tool on surveillance, and readiness for preparedness & response to outbreaks, developed and deployed to assess 5 H/Facilities & DHOs. - Rapid Assessment carried out in selected health facilities in Kampala & Mukono, border points in Malaba, Elegu & Mpondwe, and DDMCs of Tororo, Amuru & Kasese. The report highlighted major challenges to DRM and gives key policy recommendations to enhance preparedness and response to natural disasters like floods and other PHEs like COVID-19 and Ebola.
b) USD 25,200 Grant was provided and transferred to UVRI to enable the achievement of results in (1)
2) The following results were attained towards strengthening national coordination capacities for emergency response and recovery - A draft Knowledge Management Strategy for the National Emergency Coordination and Operations Centre is in place. - A multidisciplinary team of four specialists (2 Disaster Risk and Resilience, 1 Knowledge Management, and 1 Emergency Communications Specialist) forming a core team to activate a think tank in NECOC was established and in place. - Policy brief on Rapid Assessment Report Summary Findings - highlighting key findings, best practices, and policy recommendations for Health & DRM sectors and Institutional recommendations for MoH, UVRI, Health Facilities, OPM/NECOC, DLGs, UNDP and other Partners. - Policy Brief - Strengthening Uganda’s emergency response and recovery capacity for COVID-19 was finalized and disseminated through training of health workers in sentinel surveillance sites. - Finalised and disseminated the SERRU Briefing Note for OPM Management. - Finalized and disseminated guidance Notes and Reporting formats for the three Rapid Assessment tools. - Finalized proposal/concept note drafted to scale-up SERRU Project gains e.g. to support the operationalization & digitization of the RNA tools, and support development of an integrated emergency / disaster management system for OPM.
(d) A multi-sector strategy to inform capacity development for disaster risk reduction and mitigation was developed, finalized and widely disseminated.
(e) A USD 40,000 grant was extended to Makerere University towards supporting the research Agenda and members of the think-tank. As a result, six (6) research reports and policy briefs were finalized. These covered areas of: 1. Socio-economic determinants of health in Uganda 2. Health seeking behaviour and experiences with health service delivery during peak and non-peak periods of the COVID-19 pandemic in Uganda. 3. COVID-19 vaccination in Uganda: Community perceptions, vaccination management, coverage demographics and experiences with the service provision. 4. Data and Information management: Systems and tools for effective disaster risk communication. 5. Transmission dynamics of COVID-19 in space and time over Uganda: Hotspots and Brightspots controls 6. Disaster risk governance under COVID-19 at multiple scales in Uganda.
